behaviors.description: Force redeployment even when repository objects are intact.
behaviors.preconditions: App A installed, then executable unlinked only from its publicly queried deployment location.
behaviors.expected: Ordinary repair leaves the app unable to run. Repair --reinstall-all restores independent executable bytes, exact commits and execution of A.

behaviors.description: Restore a deployed app whose required repository payload is missing.
behaviors.preconditions: Independent app A and runtime installed; adapter removes the app executable object from isolated repository storage.
behaviors.expected: Repair restores the expected refs and commits, and the app can be redeployed without pulling and executed as A.

behaviors.description: Report missing repository content without changing persistent installation state.
behaviors.preconditions: Healthy dry-run baseline followed by adapter-controlled removal of the deployed app executable object.
behaviors.expected: Dry-run identifies the affected app and differs from healthy output while preserving paths, contents, ownership and modes; real repair then permits offline redeployment and execution.

mappings.rationale: Deployment-only damage leaves the repository healthy, so successful recovery requires forced redeployment.

surface_assertions.rationale: Ordinary repair does not restore execution after deployment-only unlink; forced repair restores exact independent executable bytes and execution.

mappings.rationale: Missing executable payload is injected through the reference adapter; public offline reinstall and execution prove repair restored required repository content. Exact independent app/runtime commits bracket offline redeployment.
Damaged dry-run output identifies the app and differs from a healthy control; before/after persistent installation snapshots match. Real repair subsequently restores offline redeployment.

notes: Backend-specific payload removal and persistent-state snapshots belong to the reference adapter. Other adapters may supply BLACKBOX_REPAIR_FIXTURE with the same Python invocation protocol or report the prerequisite unavailable.

Snapshots compare relative paths, file types, modes, ownership, symlink targets and file hashes. They exclude timestamps, which can change through reads, and make no inode-identity claim. Repair success is established through public CLI operations rather than backend inspection.
